sentences.text:
1
 The Honourable Sri Justice E.V. Venugopal
 Criminal Petition No.9454 Of 2023
O R D E R:

The present Criminal Petition is filed seeking to call for the records in C.C.No.751 of 2014 and quash the order dated 21.06.2023 in Crl.M.P.No.330 of 2023 in C.C.No.751 of 2014 on the file of the learned Principal Junior Civil Judge-cum-VIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally (for short, "the trial Court").
2.

Heard Mr.Apurva M. Gokhale, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr.E.Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1-State and Mr.M.Govind Reddy, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between petitioner and respondent No.2 was performed on 22.11.1998; that they were blessed with a female child during their wedlock; that after marriage the petitioner suffered harassment at the hands of respondent No.2 and his parents.

Unable to bear such harassment, she filed C.C.No.751 of 2014 against respondent No.2 for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 376(A) and 377 of Indian Penal Code; a case under Section 498-A of I.P.C. against accused Nos.2 and 3 before the competent criminal Court.

While so,
respondent No.2 filed a petition under Section 311 of Cr.P.C. seeking to re-call PW1 for further cross- examination.
The trial Court vide order dated 21.06.2023 allowed the said application on payment of Rs.3,000/- towards costs.
Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner preferred the present Criminal Petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the calendar case was reserved for judgment on 08.03.2023; that respondent No.2, on 01.06.2023, filed an application under Section 311 of Cr.P.C.
while giving notice to the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor.
He states that no notice was served upon the petitioner and the trial Court posted the case 'for orders' on 21.06.2023.

He contends that no reasonable opportunity of hearing was afforded to the petitioner to oppose the same and file counter affidavit; that the trial Court had passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner,
without assigning valid reasons.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner further contends that this Court vide order dated 14.12.2022 in Crl.P.No.4807 of 2022, set aside the order dated 27.06.2022 in Crl.M.P.No.919 of 2022 in C.C.No.751 of 2014 passed by the trial Court wherein and whereby, the trial Court had allowed an application filed by respondent No.2 and others under Section 311 of Cr.P.C. seeking to reopen the evidence of PW1.

Therefore, he contends that respondent No.2 had filed another application under Smt.Rozy Kaur vs The State Of Telangana on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93333994/
1 Section 311 of Cr.P.C. only to protract the litigation on one pretext or the other and the learned Judge of the trial Court had erroneously allowed the same by imposing costs.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he seeks to allow the Criminal Petition.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that no prejudice will be caused to PW1 if she is re-called once again for the purpose of further cross-examination.
Therefore, he submits that interference of this Court is not warranted and seeks to dismiss this Criminal Petition.

7. Having regard to the submissions of both the learned counsel and on perusal of the order dated 14.12.2022 passed by this Court in Crl.P.No.4807 of 2022, it is apparent that this Court had already directed the trial Court to conclude the proceedings in C.C.No.751 of 2014 expeditiously as the case pertains to the year, 2014.
Therefore, the trial Court ought to have re-opened the calendar case if so required, for further arguments rather than passing the impugned order.
Re-calling PW1 for further cross- examination, after reserving the calendar case for judgment would ultimately result in delay in dispensing justice.

Hence, the order dated 21.06.2023 in Crl.M.P.No.330 of 2023 in C.C.No.751 of 2014 on the file of the learned Principal Junior Civil Judge- cum-VIII Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally is set aside.

8. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is allowed.
Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
